description: Located in Noordwijk, ESTEC is a hub for the European Space Agency's activities. Given the size and complexity of the construction phases ESA plans to procure, viaa single contract, services for Project Management, Design and Engineering, Project Supervision during the implementation of the project. The Project Management services will be in support to the ESA project manager during the entirety of the project. The Design and Engineering of each of the phases will consist in the production of the engineering packages necessary to issue the tenders for construction and demolition and to support the project with any technical issues arising during the construction. The Project supervision services will be rendered during the construction and demolition phases to monitor compliance of the execution with the design and engineering specifications. ESA intends to select the Contractor in a 2-stage procurement approach. In Stage 1, the Agency shall issue a Call for Expression of Interest' open to all bidders within the ESA Members States, leading to the pre-selection of three bidders to participate in the "Restricted Competition" (Stage 2), which will finally lead to the selection of the Contractor.

title: NAVISP-EL1-107-ULTRA-HIGH SPATIAL RESOLUTION GNSS RECEIVER FOR AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: The ability of exploiting the spatial dimensions has allowed array antennas to be exploited in various applications, e.g., multipath and interference mitigation; spatial diversity; and localization. Consequently, over the past years, array antennas have been deployed in GNSS receivers either to provide a spatial filter or to improve the SNR level using beamforming techniques. In order to achieve a high spatial resolution, a large array antenna aperture should be used. The manufacturing process of a large array antenna aperture, with fully synchronized and phase-coherent radio frequency (RF) chains, is very expensive and complex. Therefore, increasing the array antenna aperture, using a limited amount of antenna elements, is the main objective of this activity. In this activity weproposed a moving array antenna instead of a single antenna receiver. By exploiting the vehicle movement, the aperture of the arrayantenna (with a limited number of antennas) can be virtually expanded to provide the virtual effect of hundreds of antennas.
